name: The Dundee Arms
address: 339 Cambridge Heath Road, Bethnal Green, London
summary: A pub on Cambridge Heath Road in Bethnal Green, open since April 2015, that advertises guest DJs, craft beer and sport on screen.

music.notes: The pub's site advertises music and guest DJs but names no styles or regular nights.

accessibility.notes: CAMRA's entry notes steps at the entrance and says the main toilets are upstairs, with no accessible toilet.

story.opened: Reopened on 2 April 2015, according to CAMRA and the pub's own website.
story.then: CAMRA's entry says the pub came back under a lease with no brewery tie, run as a sister to the Crooked Billet, and that the refurbishment uncovered an old mosaic sign. Londonist's 2015 review also placed it in the same stable as the Crooked Billet in Clapton.
story.now: The venue's own website says it opens until 1am from Thursday to Saturday. CAMRA's entry says it serves two changing cask ales.
worth_knowing: CAMRA calls the original "Dundee Arms" mosaic sign, found during the refurbishment, wonderful and very rare.
It faces York Hall, where CAMRA's entry says the Pigs Ear Beer Festival began in 1983.

story_research.note: Used own site, CAMRA and Londonist. No vibe: the only description of the room is Londonist's 2015 review, over five years old. Pubology hints at older pub history (directories from 1805) but is not clear enough to quote.
